kept.excerpt: President Donald Trump said on August 18 that talks between the United States and Iran were neither taking place nor scheduled. Iran's top negotiator said reopening the Strait of Hormuz required the United States to lift its blockade of Iranian ports, lift oil sanctions, release frozen assets, and end threats and military operations on all fronts. The June memorandum's 60-day negotiating period had elapsed on Monday, and Trump said he had no plans to extend it.
kept.relevance: Provides cutoff-day diplomatic status and identifies oil-sanctions relief as an unresolved condition for reopening Hormuz.

kept.excerpt: OFAC designated Titan Exchange for materially assisting Shahr Bank and Alps International for operating in Iran's financial sector. Treasury described Shahr Bank and its associated companies as helping Iran retrieve overseas oil-sale revenues for petroleum exporters including the National Iranian Oil Company and Naftiran Intertrade Co. Treasury said it remained committed to maximum pressure and targeting Iran's ability to generate, move, and repatriate funds.
kept.relevance: Documents a recent official enforcement action against oil-revenue channels and Treasury's stated policy direction as of the cutoff.

kept.excerpt: Effective July 7, 2026, General License X was revoked and superseded in its entirety by General License X1. X1 authorized transactions ordinarily incident and necessary to winding down previously authorized transactions through 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on July 17, with payments to blocked persons required to enter blocked, interest-bearing U.S. accounts. Except for necessary wind-down activity, it did not authorize new transactions, including purchases or loading of Iranian-origin products on or after July 7.
kept.publisher: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Office of Foreign Assets Control
kept.relevance: Establishes the operative revocation and wind-down limits against which a subsequent qualifying relief mechanism would need to be assessed.
